# Core API v1

[English](README.md) | [日本語](../../../ja/api/v1/README.md) | [Français](../../../fr/api/v1/README.md) | [中文](../../../api/v1/README.md)

Core provides commands, queries, and incremental sync for the local owner. The [operation catalog](../../../api/v1/operations.json) lists all routes; [JSON Schema](../../../api/v1/schema.json), [OpenAPI 3.1](../../../api/v1/openapi.json), and [TypeScript DTOs](../../../../src/pi_secretary/src/api/contracts.ts) define the public contract. [CoreClient](../../../../src/pi_secretary/src/core-client.ts) wraps discovery and requests. [Examples](../../../api/v1/examples.json) and [Swift decoding examples](../../../api/v1/decode-examples.swift) demonstrate string precision, Unicode, and extension-field handling.

## Connection and authentication

Start Core using the [operations guide](../../operations.md). It listens on a dynamic `127.0.0.1` port. The data directory’s `core-endpoint.json` (0600) stores address, token, instance_id, and mode. CoreClient verifies file ownership, permissions, and mode. owner/data_domain_id persist across restarts; instance_id changes at every startup.

Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and optionally `X-Secretary-API-Version: 1`. Host must match the discovered address; Origin, if present, must also match. Authentication establishes a local-owner principal; ClientRegistration registers the presenting client identity. All routes use `/api/v1`.

## Commands and receipts

POST uses application/json with a maximum body of 1 MiB and a UUID request_id. The owner, path, and normalized body bind the intent. Resubmitting the same ID and parameters returns the original receipt; changed content returns REQUEST_CONFLICT. HTTP 202 means admission is durable; `GET requests/{id}` returns the receipt, while related resources report domain progress.

Short commands commit ApiCommand with the first domain change in one transaction and normally remain ACCEPTED; even no-op commands save a NO_CHANGES receipt. Long commands move from QUEUED to RUNNING, then COMPLETED or UNKNOWN. Restart resumes unstarted QUEUED work and marks interrupted RUNNING work UNKNOWN for reconciliation against domain receipts. `memory/extraction/retry` is short; extraction retries continue in the background.

| Result received | Client action |
| --- | --- |
| Command POST 400/404/409/410/413/422 | Submission was rejected before admission; for REQUEST_CONFLICT, retain the existing receipt for the original ID |
| 202 | Save the receipt and query related resources |
| Timeout, disconnect, 5xx | Query the original request_id; reconcile if a receipt exists. Resubmit the original ID, path, and body only after explicit NOT_FOUND and with no local admitted/UNKNOWN evidence |
| 401/403 | Correct authentication or request origin before proceeding |

Domain errors after admission retain the receipt. The rejection rules above apply to command POSTs; handle GET query errors according to their error codes.

## Queries, pagination, and content

Responses use `{api_version:"1",data:...}`; errors use `{api_version:"1",error:{code,message}}`. revision, event sequence, World version, and byte lengths are decimal strings; counts and limit are bounded integers; timestamps are UTC ISO 8601. Requests are schema-validated; clients decode known response fields.

Assistant names are trimmed for display. An empty name projects as `Secretary`; an explicitly configured `secretary` keeps its lowercase spelling. This is a projection default, not a stored-profile migration.

Ordinary lists default to 30 entries, maximum 100. A cursor binds the instance, query scope/filters, and last stable key; changing limit can continue, but CURSOR_EXPIRED requires reloading. Lists paginate by stable keys such as first transaction position and ID; sync fills changes. Timeline, message content, and World have their own cursor semantics. GET reads state; a separate viewed command extends HOT retention when users view execution details.

| Content | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| timeline | At most 200 items within a 1 MiB page; around locates by message_id or event_id; short reasoning previews are included by default; streaming/thinking control body expansion, merged with final messages by call_id |
| messages/{id}/content | Follow next_cursor for Unicode chunks |
| operations/{id} | display contains parameters/stdout/stderr/reason with state, bytes, content_version, truncated, next_cursor, unavailable_reason; first chunks are capped at 16/32/32/4 KiB respectively, full detail at 256 KiB |
| operations/{id}/content | part selects a section above; cursor continues reading; each chunk ≤32 KiB, response ≤256 KiB; concatenate in order before parsing JSON; on CURSOR_EXPIRED, restart from the first chunk |
| artifacts | Download fixed CAS bytes by artifact ID and verify hash and length; relative_path, path_base, scope_id provide safe relative locations; missing bindings are marked unknown |

Operation bytes/hash refer to the full public text. source_truncated means the executor truncated source output; pagination truncated means more content follows this page. Resolved stdout/stderr retain original receipts; reason.resolution_note explains the resolution. Public projections preserve domain JSON but remove internal shell environments, program entrypoints/workspaces, and internal CAS locations. Missing, corrupt, or unsafe sources return an unavailable reason. See [operation-display](../../../../src/pi_secretary/src/operation-display.ts).

## Domain resources

| Resource | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| assistant/profile, messages, session | Display name, input, compaction, and recovery |
| tasks, task-requests, executions | Task baseline, per-round proposals, queuing/cancellation, results, and continuations; tasks supports scope_id filtering, with none for no scope binding |
| scopes, authorizations, authorization-rules, decisions, operations | Work scopes, approvals/rules, work-related answers, and effect verification |
| settings, memory, memory/summary, memory/commitments | Draft application, maintenance progress, summaries, and commitment provenance |
| world/catalog, world/facts, world/slot | Entities/predicate/source, current and historical facts, slot revision |
| related, attention | Related resources, pending counts, and bounded lists; attention provides version/as_of/valid_until |
| requests, clients, core, admin | Receipts, client registration, service lifecycle, World migrations, and program registration |

PublicTaskCommand uses an `acceptance` string array. Continuations supply both reuse_task_id and parent_execution_id; see [task data flow](../../data-flow.md#from-task-proposal-to-result). Settings stores full instructions/edits/command_ids and uses expected_revision for version control. New World resources have revision "0"; a domain batch allows at most 50 items (the public structure allows 100).

## Master attention (#92)

`GET attention?view=master` returns unexpired approvals, actionable questions, unresolved execution failures, unresolved current initialization failures and unknown outcomes; omitting `view` preserves the existing behavior. The complete set is ordered by immutable initiation time and sequence descending and paged with signed cursors; counts cover the full set. Core computes failure categories and `cause_evidence`. Reminder membership follows explicit FailureHandling dispositions and directly linked redo outcomes; unrelated success never implies resolution.

`GET failures/{failure_key}` reads the exact failure, current intent and linked redo status without writes. Execution keys are `EXECUTION:<id>`; initialization keys are `TASK_INIT:<task_id>:<episode_sequence>`. Legacy failures default to revision `0` and UNRESOLVED. `POST messages` accepts `failure_action: {failure_key, expected_revision, action: "REDO" | "DISMISS"}` with empty text and no attachments. Core atomically admits Input, FailureHandling and the API receipt and generates fixed metadata text. An identical request_id replays exactly; a different payload conflicts. Pending intents, active redos, stale revisions and resolved failures produce their respective 409 errors. REDO authorizes Main to continue only the original Task/parent with unchanged requirements; DISMISS removes only that reminder. Each FAILED/CANCELLED RESULT feedback has its own Main batch and cannot autonomously task_propose; EXPIRED retains its existing policy.

`Execution.failure` provides the category, recorded reason, linked authorization and operation, and their actual states. A rejection cause requires reciprocal records and a persisted decision frame before the failure; inconsistent or unavailable evidence is explicit. `TaskPlan` changes invalidate attention, and clients must also refresh at `valid_until`.

## Scopes, authorization, and effect resolution

Scope creation requires name/kind. DIRECTORY points to an existing physical root_path; notes_path defaults to `.secretary/NOTES.md`. NONE gives each task a private directory. Updates/archiving require expected_revision; archiving preserves history and occupied executions. Execution freezes its creation-time binding. condition_results returns MET/NOT_MET/UNKNOWN with evidence; directory conditions may return SCOPE_BUSY, SCOPE_ARCHIVED, or SCOPE_ROOT_CONFLICT.

`default_write=allow|ask` defaults to allow. Submit approval through `authorizations/{id}/decision` with expected_revision, display_hash, and APPROVE/REJECT/REVOKE. APPROVE may include remember, such as `{prefix_tokens:2,expires_at:null}` for shell or `{path_prefix:"src",expires_at:null}` for write. remember_context supplies the root and original parameters for display; the server commits authorization and the rule atomically. After revoking an individual authorization, persistent rules can be disabled separately through admin/authorization-rules/{id}/disable.

Rules support either legacy exact parameters matching or file-prefix, command-prefix, or program constraints, with optional valid_from/expires_at. world.change uses exact parameters. GET authorization-rules returns rules and builtin_policies; match_count/last_matched_at count unique Operations whose dispatch committed successfully. Built-in read-only commands run with fixed argv; user shell-prefix rules still use bash. See [shell-policy](../../../../src/pi_secretary/src/shell-policy.ts).

`operations/{id}/resolve` accepts request_id, expected_revision, outcome, and note; outcome is APPLIED/NOT_APPLIED/PARTIAL/UNVERIFIED. `verify-write` verifies the file against the bound root and expected content. Effect resolution, handling of other unknowns, and process termination together determine execution finalization. Details expose effect, resolution, and process_state.

## Incremental sync

First GET sync/cursor to obtain S, then load resources, then catch up with GET sync/changes?after=S and connect sync/stream. A cursor binds owner_id, transaction sequence, and journal digest, and survives normal restarts. A new data domain, truncated backup, or divergent history returns 409 RESYNC_REQUIRED; reload while retaining original commands for reconciliation.

changes examines 100 transactions by default and at most 100, including transactions with no public changes. It returns transactions, next_cursor, and has_more, capped at 256 KiB per page. Transactions are delivered whole; oversized ones become invalidate entries for all relevant categories. record carries resource_type/resource_id/revision; invalidate requires refreshing the specified aggregate or collection even if its root revision is unchanged. Pagination version is the observed watermark.

SSE sends event: change per transaction, with the post-transaction cursor as id; empty changes still advance it. Comment heartbeats arrive about every 5 seconds; transient previews/activity have no id. If both after and Last-Event-ID are supplied, they must agree. Clients advance their cursor only after atomically persisting refreshed data and the applied watermark, keep the result of the most recently initiated refresh, and retain pending-refresh status if that refresh fails. Per connection: 512 KiB pending-write budget, at most 5 seconds to drain, at most 8 streams. Slow connections disconnect and resume from the applied watermark. See [sync-service](../../../../src/pi_secretary/src/sync-service.ts) and [sync-stream](../../../../src/pi_secretary/src/sync-stream.ts).

## Notifications, reminders, and push delivery

notifications returns the global collection. presented is the first presentation per client; read_at is the global first read. created_sequence fixes creation position; notifications before the initial watermark load as history, and subsequent read/presented updates retain that position. Notification content inlines text/media_type/content_version/bytes/truncated, capped at 2 KiB per list item and 64 KiB in detail; truncated JSON is displayed as text.

`notifications/{id}/presented` carries request_id/client_id; the client must be registered in this data domain. Presentation event and admission commit together; repeats return the original record or NO_CHANGES. `notifications/{id}/read` carries only request_id and preserves the first read_at. Both are independent of channel status; receipt processing triggers neither Input nor a model call.

wakeups supports lists, details, and `{id}/cancel`, with state filters PENDING/FIRED/CANCELLED; creation uses the main-session tool. Cancellation changes only PENDING; FIRED means TIMER Input is queued. Creation, firing, and cancellation enter ChangeFeed. Recovery catches up overdue items; the main session decides whether to notify. See [server-side push delivery](push.md) for targets, private configuration, quiet hours, and retries.

## Current limitations

- Notification content is bounded inline text; a paginated notification-body endpoint is not yet available.
- The public wakeups API supports queries and cancellation; creation uses the main session’s schedule_wakeup tool.

See the [operations guide](../../operations.md) for upgrades and validation, and [historical validation records](../../../api/v1/verification.md) for version-specific acceptance.

## FE-04 Message projection

Message projections may include provenance, original event IDs, direct related IDs, outcomes and preview availability, derived only from existing records. A saved preview does not imply durable success; expiry only means transient display content is unavailable.

Optional fields: `source_kind`, `source_event_id`, `outcome`, `preview_availability`, `request_id`, `task_id`, `execution_id`, `result_id`, `decision_request_id`, `notification_id`. See the authored `Message` schema for enum values.

## Response outcomes and reasoning previews

Empty abnormal replies retain a message row: length/error/aborted project to truncated/failed/interrupted with incomplete=true; normal empty stop and tool-only replies remain omitted. An empty error projects to interrupted only for a non-colliding same-session ModelCall explicitly marked INTERRUPTED/CANCELLED. If a historical empty abnormal reply reuses an occupied display_call_id, it uses its own event ID and call_id=null.

A length-limited model activity is truncated live, historically and after restart, with phase `输出已截断`; ModelCall remains RESPONSE_SAVED and parent business states are unchanged.

thinking_preview is an optional `{text,truncated}` display field. It joins nonempty, non-redacted thinking blocks in source order with newlines and retains the first 20 extended grapheme clusters; when content is omitted and the prefix is nonempty, one U+2026 is appended. JSON-encoded text, including the ellipsis, is at most 4 KiB without splitting clusters; an oversized first cluster yields empty text and truncated=true. It returns no signatures, invents no reasoning and changes neither model input nor identity.

Default timeline, around, message content and SSE transient provide the same short preview. Full reasoning requires thinking=true; transient bodies additionally require streaming=true. Hidden reasoning produces no continuation cursor, so reasoning-only messages default to next_cursor=null. Explicit expansion paginates at Unicode scalar boundaries: each body or reasoning fragment is at most 4,999 UTF-16 units and 28,000 JSON bytes, with a 64 KiB whole-message fragment bound. Preview truncated, retained-message truncation and outcome=truncated have separate meanings.

SSETransient/SSEPreview define the public transient shape; Preview.version remains a number and the event has no durable cursor. The short preview is computed before retention clipping. Redaction, including done/error snapshots, revokes retained reasoning and advances revision; old content cursors return CURSOR_EXPIRED. Main retains at most 8 previews; Task independently retains at most 32 previews and 1 MiB of text in total. Each preview permits 128 blocks and 32,768 UTF-16 units. Normal redacted-only/tool-only durable replies may still omit a row, so transient expiry does not prove the absence of a durable event.

thinking_preview and thinking preserve raw model text, which may contain control characters or ANSI sequences. Terminal clients must escape or sanitize it before rendering; the API does not perform terminal-safety processing for clients.

For imports, budget profiles, K=0 residency and safe withdrawal, see the [attachment contract](attachments.md).

## Issue #94 artifact delivery

Artifact metadata adds result_id, nullable description (Task model / NOT_VERIFIED), source_root, current_path, current_state, observed_at and current_unavailable_reason. Read-only paths use the originating Execution.workspace_binding; missing historical bindings remain unavailable. Snapshot state/content_version/bytes retain their existing meaning. No Scope lookup may create a directory during projection.

GET artifacts accepts exact canonical relative_path and optional execution_id, filters to accessible tasks before CAS/current-file observations and paginates matching metadata. Unicode normalization is a comparison alias only; distinct physical paths remain ambiguous for clients. GET messages/{id}/artifacts resolves the visible, owned Main reply's durable references in registration order. Pages contain at most 20 entries and 128 KiB, shrinking count without truncating an entry; cursors are opaque and message-bound. Timeline/message delivery_count exposes the total and delivery_cursor is null for the first page.

The main.delivery event is an ID-only sidecar to an unchanged main.message event, committed atomically with the Context pointer. Only RESULT feedback CLAIMED by that Main loop supplies references. Stop/length replies without tool calls may carry delivery, including empty bodies; length stays truncated. Queries, previews, tool continuations and failed replies do not create delivery. Existing stop-only crash recovery is unchanged.

New submit_result artifacts remain a path array and require exactly one artifact_descriptions item per nonempty registered path. Paths canonicalize dot segments and reject traversal/control/duplicates; limits are 32 artifacts, 2000 Unicode characters per explanation and 64 KiB total encoded descriptions. Legacy stored results remain readable without descriptions. Host generates Artifact IDs and binds explanations before publishing the result.

## Exact execution guidance (#103)

`POST executions/{execution_id}/guidance` accepts `{request_id, task_id, text}` for a nonterminal AGENT execution in the current data domain. Authentication supplies identity; callers cannot declare sources or receipts. Limits are 16,384 UTF-8 bytes per instruction, 64 instructions and 65,536 original bytes per execution. Excess returns 413 (GUIDANCE_TOO_LARGE / GUIDANCE_LIMIT_REACHED), creating neither Guidance nor an informational Input. Text is never truncated or split. Blank text is rejected; all other text is preserved exactly.

Admission atomically stores Guidance, one informational Master Input and the original request receipt. Main task_control guide uses the same domain service without a self-notification copy. Identical retries recover the original result even after termination; changed arguments or targets return REQUEST_CONFLICT. Reconcile uncertain responses using the original request_id; never resend under a new identity or retarget latest.

`GET guidance/{id}` exposes original text, source, SENT/RECEIVED/GUIDED timestamps, disposition and actual ModelCall receipts. `GET executions/{id}/guidance?limit=20&cursor=...` paginates in admission order with limit 1–100. SENT means durable acceptance; RECEIVED requires host injection in a durable checkpoint; GUIDED requires an actual model request and valid ADOPTED receipt. A steer call, UI display or HTTP 202 does not prove adoption.

Accepted guidance must enter the next eligible fresh model request. An older in-flight or frozen response is blocked so a fresh turn can consume it. If an included instruction still has no valid disposition when success is attempted, fail immediately with GUIDANCE_NOT_PROCESSED; there is no three-response grace period. Valid conflict or inability to adopt creates a deduplicated DecisionRequest; Main cannot answer required_answerer=MASTER.

Guidance during WAIT_AUTH leaves authorization pending. Approval retires obsolete operations that have not started, then replans and rechecks authorization. Denial still fails execution. Authorization details expose guidance_warning explaining this behavior. Waiting questions are not automatically answered, unknown effects are not replayed, and cancellation never revives execution to consume guidance. Failure, cancellation and expiry settle unprocessed guidance with a retained reason.

This issue provides the backend and existing matter notices. Task streaming, stable titles/rounds and the `/guide` command are delivered by #104, #105 and #106 respectively.

## Task streaming and latest tails (#104)

Task previews are disposable, unsaved display state. SSE sends an independent metadata-only Task frame (at most 64 KiB) with epoch/version and exact task, execution, ModelCall, attempt and status; it contains no body or thinking. Main transient size cannot suppress it. Clients fetch only the affected Task message. Token deltas create no journal transaction, Main Input, ordinary progress Feedback or Main model call. Durable ModelCall and agent-message facts continue to invalidate timeline/activity history and additionally invalidate the exact Task-message query.

Task message routes accept `position=latest`; content tails expose `body_offset`, `body_length`, `thinking_offset`, `thinking_length` and at most 32,768 UTF-16 units per region. A missing format prefix must be labeled and rendered literally; normal cursor paging still reads full durable content. Message IDs use `call:<model_call_id>` only with proven provenance; legacy event IDs remain aliases or original rows. `persistence=transient` and `preview_status` distinguish unsaved output from durable response. Missing previews from an older runtime or ended execution report interruption, never indefinite waiting or fabricated saved text. Encode message IDs as URL path segments. Existing owner, retention and latest-three-executions checks apply to queries and SSE visibility.

### Task identity and exact execution lookup (#105)

`TaskCommand.title_candidate` is an optional creation-only advisory name; null is omission. Core allocates an immutable NFC title, unique across the entire data root, including archived tasks. Reuse with a non-null candidate fails with `TITLE_ON_REUSE_NOT_ALLOWED`; REDO retains its existing requirements guard. Candidate inputs are limited to 1,024 UTF-8 bytes; allocated names are bounded to 64 Unicode scalars / 256 bytes, including collision suffixes. No additional model call is made.

Task and Execution projections expose `title` and permanent `execution_round` values. Recent-three ordering does not renumber them. UUIDs remain protocol identities and workspace names.

- `GET task-browser/locate?selector_kind=title|id|auto&selector=...` locates an exact title or unique ID prefix. Auto uses the union and rejects ambiguity. Legacy `task_id`/`match` remains ID-only; do not combine the two forms.
- `GET task-browser/suggestions?selector_kind=auto&selector=...&limit=20` returns bounded typed suggestions with titles, task IDs, states and recent execution IDs/rounds/states.
- `GET task-browser/resolve?selector_kind=title&selector=...&execution_round=7&purpose=browse|guidance` returns exact immutable IDs and snapshot revisions. Rounds must be positive ASCII integers without leading zeros. No latest fallback, business command or liveness reservation is created. Session, active-scope and recent-three visibility apply. Guidance purpose also rejects ended, cancelling, PROGRAM and RESULT_UNKNOWN targets. Final guidance admission rechecks the frozen IDs; existing accepted receipt replay is retained. Already-started archived work keeps its existing exact-ID guidance capability.

Startup performs a resumable, append-only identity migration before business recovery. This is a one-way format upgrade. Before starting an upgraded binary on a real root, stop its writer, back up the complete root, and verify an isolated copy can reopen. Preserve the backup; never run an older binary against the upgraded root or overwrite newer work automatically. Migration uses committed creation order, preserves old references and assigned identities, and emits a durable completion event. No migration of a live user root is part of automated verification.
